title: Why your brain may be sabotaging your balance as you age
summary: Balance problems in aging and Parkinson’s may come from the body working too hard, not too little. Scientists found that the brain and muscles become overactive during even minor disturbances, yet this actually weakens balance recovery. title: Fathers face rising depression risk a year after baby arrives
summary: New fathers appear to have fewer mental health diagnoses during pregnancy and the early months after birth. But that early stability does not last. title: Fatty liver breakthrough: A common vitamin shows promise
summary: Researchers have identified microRNA-93 as a key genetic driver of fatty liver disease and discovered that vitamin B3 can effectively shut it down. This finding suggests a safe, widely available vitamin could become a powerful new treatment.

summary: Researchers have developed a teeth-whitening powder that works with the vibrations of an electric toothbrush to safely remove stains. summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising brain-based trigger for high blood pressure, tracing it to a small region in the brainstem that normally controls breathing. summary: GLP-1 medications like semaglutide (Ozempic) may offer unexpected mental health benefits alongside weight loss. title: New pill cuts “bad” cholesterol by 60% in major trial
summary: A new pill, enlicitide, reduced LDL (“bad”) cholesterol by about 60% in a large clinical trial, matching the power of injectable therapies. Because it’s taken orally, it could overcome one of the biggest barriers keeping patients from using current treatments. title: These “forever chemicals” could be weakening kids’ bones for life
summary: “Forever chemicals” may be affecting kids in ways that last a lifetime. A new study links early PFAS exposure to lower bone density during the teen years, especially in girls. Researchers also found that when exposure happens may play a key role. Reducing exposure during childhood could help protect long-term bone health.

title: Huge study finds no evidence cannabis helps anxiety, depression, or PTSD
summary: The largest review of medicinal cannabis to date found it doesn’t effectively treat anxiety, depression, or PTSD—despite millions using it for those reasons. title: This common vaccine cuts heart risk nearly in half in new study
summary: A shingles vaccine might double as a powerful heart protector. In people already at high risk, it cut major cardiac events by 46% and deaths by an impressive 66% within a year. title: This virus therapy supercharges the immune system against brain cancer
summary: Scientists have found a way to make one of the most aggressive brain tumors vulnerable to the immune system. A single injection of a modified virus can invade glioblastoma, kill cancer cells, and summon immune fighters deep into the tumor. These immune cells persist and attack, which was linked to longer survival in patients.

summary: A common oral bacterium tied to gum disease may help spark and fuel breast cancer, according to new research. summary: Eating large amounts of ultra-processed foods like chips, frozen meals, sugary drinks, and packaged snacks may significantly raise the risk of serious heart problems. title: Belly fat linked to heart failure risk even in people with normal weight
summary: Carrying extra fat around the waist may be more dangerous than the number on the scale suggests. title: Cutting sweet foods doesn’t reduce cravings or improve health
summary: A new study suggests that eating less sweet food doesn’t make people crave it any less—or improve their health markers. title: You don’t need to lose weight to reverse prediabetes, study finds
summary: For years, people with prediabetes have been told the same thing: lose weight or risk developing diabetes. summary: Cycling might be one of the simplest ways for older adults to stay healthier, longer. title: Your daily coffee may be protecting your brain, 43-year study finds
summary: Your morning coffee or tea could be quietly supporting your brain health. title: Scientists link childhood stress to lifelong digestive issues
summary: Early life stress may set the stage for long-term digestive problems by disrupting the gut-brain connection. title: Scientists finally reveal how this Alzheimer’s drug really works
summary: A key Alzheimer’s drug has finally revealed its secret. Researchers discovered that lecanemab works by activating the brain’s immune cells—but only through a specific part of the antibody called the Fc fragment. title: ADHD brains show sleep-like activity even while awake
summary: Researchers have identified a surprising brain pattern that may help explain why people with ADHD often struggle to stay focused. Even while awake, their brains can slip into brief episodes of “sleep-like” activity during demanding tasks. These moments are linked to more mistakes, slower reaction times, and lapses in attention.
